_meta.description: Haulage economics between the farm gate and an industrial cleaner plus optical sorter (trieur optique). This is the layer that turns 'no sorter within 80 km' from a flag into a cost, and therefore the layer that makes a 'stranded' parcel a financial category rather than a label.
_meta.why_it_matters: To be sold for human consumption a pulse lot must pass an industrial cleaner and an optical sorter. The nearest unit sets a haulage bill that is paid per tonne of FOOD-grade harvest. Far enough away and it consumes the entire food premium, which is the precise mechanism by which agronomically ideal land stays in cereals.
_meta.attribution_rule: Only the INCREMENTAL haul is charged. A farm already hauls its cereals to a local silo and that cost is inside the RICA operating cost the finance engine uses, so charging the full farm-to-sorter distance would double-count the first 25 km and would also unfairly penalise the pulse arm relative to the cereal arm it is compared against.

haulage.source: Bulk agricultural road haulage, 25-30 t semi-trailer, French domestic rates 2024-2025. The range spans backhaul-loaded contract work at the low end and short-distance spot haulage at the high end.
haulage.road_detour_factor_note: Great-circle distance understates road distance. 1.32 is a conventional detour ratio for the French secondary road network on rural origin-destination pairs. Applied uniformly, so it cannot flatter one site over another, but it IS an approximation: a real deployment should use a routed distance matrix.
haulage.local_collection_radius_note: Distance a farm hauls to its ordinary collection silo, already embedded in the RICA operating cost. Only distance BEYOND this is charged as incremental.
haulage.feed_outlet_radius_note: The downgraded fraction does not need sorting. It goes to a local feed compounder or a neighbouring breeder, so it is treated as inside the ordinary collection radius and carries no incremental haul.

sorting.max_distance_note: Beyond roughly 80 km of road distance the haulage bill on a 1.5-4 t/ha pulse crop consumes the food-grade premium. Used as the binary access flag; the cost model above is continuous and is what actually drives the economics.
sorting.cleaning_and_sorting_fee_note: Toll processing charged by the station on food-grade tonnage: pre-cleaning, calibration, optical sort, bagging to retail spec. Charged on the food fraction in BOTH the access and no-access cases, so it is not what creates the stranded category.
sorting.removed_note: A food_grade_loss_in_sorting_pct of 6.5 was removed. It had no source, and it was deliberately not charged anywhere in the margin (to avoid double-counting against P_human), so it was an undefendable number sitting in reference data doing nothing.

new_unit.capex_note: Turnkey industrial line sized for a cooperative silo: pre-cleaner, calibrator, optical sorter, bagging. Consistent with the order of magnitude of Planification Ecologique equipment grants for pulse sorting infrastructure.
new_unit.annual_opex_note: Energy, consumables, one operator at part load, maintenance contract.
new_unit.siting_constraint: A new unit is only sited at an existing cooperative silo or industrial platform. Greenfield siting is excluded: the capex above does not include land, three-phase power, weighbridge or reception pit, which a silo already has.
new_unit.capacity_t_yr_note: Annual throughput of one cleaning-and-optical-sorting line, and the parameter the regional headline is most sensitive to: it sets hectares-per-unit linearly, so the machine count needed to reach the area target scales inversely with it (5,000 t/yr implies about 221 units, 20,000 t/yr about 56). Basis: a single optical sorter rated at roughly 4-6 t/h on pulses, run on a single shift over the 8-10 week post-harvest campaign when pulses are actually cleaned, is of order 10,000 t. Double-shifting or a longer campaign raises it; running a second crop through the same line lowers it.
new_unit.capacity_t_yr_range_note: Single shift over a short campaign at the low end; extended shifts and a longer campaign at the high end. The engine reports machine counts across this band rather than from the point value, because the point value is a plant-configuration choice rather than a measurement.
new_unit.economic_life_yr_note: Conventional depreciation horizon for food-grade grain handling equipment. Only affects the levelised cost per tonne, not hectares unlocked.
new_unit.discount_rate_note: Public-sector style real discount rate, used because the capital in question is a regional grant rather than commercial debt. Only affects levelised cost per tonne.

regional_fund.envelope_note: Order of magnitude of a regional Planification Ecologique agricultural envelope. Used only to convert the optimiser's unit count into a budget line; it is not a committed programme.
regional_fund.max_units_fundable_note: Derived, not assumed: envelope_eur / new_unit.capex_eur. Shown so the optimiser's k slider has a budget-consistent ceiling.
